source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Only end-stage respiratory failure requiring immediate specialized intervention, rather than earlier warning signs","B":"Referral being made mainly when specifically requested by the client themselves, rather than based on clinical findings","C":"Fairly few established referral criteria actually existing to help guide when a pulmonology referral becomes appropriate","D":"Diagnostic uncertainty, inadequate symptom control despite standard treatment, or need for specialized testing or procedures"}}
source_row.rationale: Common pulmonology referral triggers include diagnostic uncertainty, inadequate symptom control despite standard treatment, or the need for specialized testing or procedures (such as bronchoscopy), generally recommended well before end-stage disease to support timely, specialized management.
source_row.source_name: American Thoracic Society — Pulmonology Referral Guidelines
